earlier_scan.source_named: Yanson, Rudolf (1990), Voprosy fonologii drevnebirmanskogo jazyka [Questions of Old Burmese Phonology] (cited on Wikipedia Old_Burmese); not retrievable

sources.note: Phonology section covers aspiration only; nothing on stress, tone, or syllable structure; reference list used to seed the search.

sources.citation: Dempsey, Jakob. 2001. Remarks on the vowel system of Old Burmese. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 24(2): 205-234. DOI 10.32655/ltba.24.2.10
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Vowels/rhymes only; no stress statement. One passing remark (p. 226, scanned text) that 'Standard Burmese tends to fuse the parts of a sesquisyllable together (e.g. kjat tiger < *kla..)'. PDF had no text layer; scanned at 200 dpi.

sources.citation: Nishi, Yoshio. 1999. Old Burmese: toward the history of Burmese [古ビルマ語：ビルマ語史へ向けて]. Bulletin of the National Museum of Ethnology 23(3): 659-692. DOI 10.15021/00004119 (English text; the article version of the Old Burmese paper in Four Papers on Burmese).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Section 1.7 'Marking of Suprasegmental Features' (p. 664) and section 4.3 'Tones' treat only tone marks (-h, visarga, devoweled letter) and the OB-to-Standard Burmese tone correspondences; the only 'atonic syllable' remark (note 1, p. 681) describes Standard Burmese transcription, not Old Burmese.

sources.citation: Wun, Maung. 1975 [issue dated 1976-03]. Development of the Burmese language in the medieval period. Osaka Gaikokugo Daigaku Gakuho 35: 63-119. https://hdl.handle.net/11094/80571
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; historical/philological survey of medieval Burmese; text-layer search for stress/accent/prosody/minor syllable returns no relevant hit.
